Kevin Garnett played basketball with an intensity that was impossible to ignore. From entering the NBA straight out of high school in 1995 to becoming an MVP in Minnesota and an NBA champion in Boston, Garnett gave everything he had to the game. The emotion, the passion, and the competitiveness became part of his identity. But behind that intensity was a person who didn’t always feel comfortable letting others see what he was feeling. There’s something interesting about that contrast. Sometimes the people who appear the toughest are the ones who have learned to keep the most to themselves. And maybe strength isn’t always about how well you hide what you’re feeling. Sometimes it’s being comfortable enough to let people see it. ⚓️ - ➸ Curious how these edits come together?
